what_happened: The agent told the person running Athena (Sri) that the "this rule is wrong" fix had been rejected by the flaky drain test. That was wrong. The rejected job was the history-rules job. The rule fix had not been rejected. A container restart had interrupted it. The agent saw a rejection line, assumed it belonged to the job it expected, and did not check which job it named. No work was judged bad.
cause: Status is read from raw log and queue lines that name a job only by id, and nothing ties a line to the job or request the reader is asking about. The agent matched a line to the job it expected and passed the guess on as fact. Athena gives no per-job status view that states each job's state and cause (rejected, interrupted, running) in one place. This is the shared cause of the other hand-command mistakes: a person or agent acts or reports on state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it.
prevention: Add a standing rule for the agent: before reporting a job's outcome, look up that job by id (state, stage and cause), and quote the id in the report. If a rejection line is found by searching, confirm that its job id matches the job being discussed. If the state can't be resolved, say so instead of inferring it. A per-job status command that shows state and reason would support this, but the rule alone would have prevented this instance.
proposed_request: Add a rule to the agent defaults for status reports. Before the agent tells the person running Athena that a job was rejected, failed, interrupted or landed, it must look up that job by id with the job status command. It must name the job id and its recorded state and cause in the report. If it found the line by searching logs, it must confirm the line's job id equals the job being discussed. When the state can't be resolved, the report must say what is unknown. Acceptance: the defaults text contains this rule, the prompt token budget test still passes, and the boundary word test passes.
